newsitem.title: IRAQ: Lloyd's in Baghdad to inspect Iraqi trade outlets.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's in Baghdad to inspect Iraqi trade outlets.

text.p: A team from Lloyd's Shipping Intelligence arrived in Baghdad on Wednesday to inspect Iraq's trade outlets.

A United Nations source said three experts under Ivor Lavers were in Baghdad for talks with Iraqi government officials prior to an inspection tour of Iraq's southern port of Umm Qasr and its border posts with both Turkey and Jordan.
Iraq on Monday accepted all U.N. conditions for the implementation of an oil-for-food deal permitting Baghdad exports of $2 billion every six months to enable it buy food and medicine.
The U.N. source said the experts would examine Iraqi facilities on the ground and pave the way for future U.N. inspection of humanitarian supplies reaching Iraq under the deal.
Lavers told reporters: "Our visit is to have discussions with the Iraqi government officials with regard to U.N. sanctions (resolution) 986."
He said he would hold his first meeting with the Iraqi authorities later on Wednesday and could travel to Basra for a fact-finding tour of Iraq's southern port of Umm Qasr on Thursday.
Resolution 986 on which the deal is based is designed to ease the suffering of the Iraqi people emanating from crippling trade sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
It provides for strict U.N. monitoring of oil sales and food distribution.
